e-5230.knowledge_point: Identifying the Parts of Cramer's Rule Formula
e-5230.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y=2 \\ 2x+y=1.\end{aligned}
$$

 
According to Cramer's rule, the unknown $x$ can be written as
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14057622/assets/2d3571405367c6d4ce15927a1dbdb50a30af7d13580c7b9cd3c73bada0583c98.png)
Express $D_x$ in terms of a $2 \times 2$ determinant.
e-5230.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y=2 \\ 2x+y=1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct $D_x$, we replace the first column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

e-4575.knowledge_point: Expressing an Unknown in Terms of 2x2 Determinants
e-4575.problem:
Consider the system of equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x+2y=-1 \\ -3x+3y=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Express $y$ in terms of $2 \times 2$ determinants.
e-4575.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x+2y=-1 \\ -3x+3y=9.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct $D_y$, we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ -3 & 9\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ -3 & 9\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-4578.knowledge_point: Solving for a Coefficient in a 2x2 Linear System Using Cramer's Rule
e-4578.problem:
Let $\langle x,3 \rangle$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x-2y=4 \\ x+ky=8\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14057622/assets/b82f5c43c9ec788b95e7213bef63eb37e4abf9d0159f92cbeedc0f64c4d35283.png)

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14057622/assets/648ce0c1b8b77c1230c6c634c676624f9c79c12ffc3942abc09d24d0fdc424d3.png)

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14057622/assets/bc7a566778813050611b098cebe221aa77ac27677e922cd282fc8ff9c3670cfd.png)
e-4578.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\dfrac{D_y}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ 1 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =5\cdot 8-4\cdot 1 \\  & =36.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D} \\ 3 & =\frac{36}{|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}|} \\ |\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}| & =12\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "II only".

According to Cramer's rule, the unknown $x$ can be written as

content.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x+2y=7 \\ 3x-4y=8.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is 

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{x}$, we replace the first column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}7 & 2 \\ 8 & -4\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x+9y=\,0 \\ \,\,\,x+2y=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the unknown $x$ can be written as  $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{|\begin{aligned}5 & 9 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|}$, where ${D}_{x}=$
after.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x+9y=\,0 \\ \,\,\,x+2y=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 9 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{x}$, we replace the first column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}\,\text{ }0 & 9 \\ \,-1 & 2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:

{\begin{aligned}\,\,3x-3y=1 \\ -x+2y=2.\end{aligned}

$$
{\begin{aligned}\,\,3x-3y=1 \\ -x+2y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the unknown $y$ can be written as $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|}$, where ${D}_{y}=$
content.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}\,\,3x-3y=1 \\ -x+2y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$, we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}3 & \,\,1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-6x+8y=-46 \\ 6x+5y=20.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}-6 & \,8 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$, we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}-6 & -46 \\ 6 & 20\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-6x+8y=-46 \\ 6x+5y=20.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}-6 & \,8 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$, we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}-6 & -46 \\ 6 & 20\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3x+11y=-23 \\ 5x-y=21.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & \,11 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$, we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & -23 \\ 5 & 21\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, $x=$
after.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+2y=12 \\ 4x+5y=21.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we construct ${D}_{x}$, we replace the first column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}12 & 2 \\ 21 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}12 & 2 \\ 21 & 5\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+2y=12 \\ 4x+5y=21.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we construct ${D}_{x}$, we replace the first column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}12 & 2 \\ 21 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}12 & 2 \\ 21 & 5\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
Consider the system of equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+8y=-14 \\ 5x+4y=13.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, $y=$
after.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+8y=-14 \\ 5x+4y=13.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 8 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$ we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -14 \\ 5 & 13\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}2 & -14 \\ 5 & 13\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}2 & 8 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+8y=-14 \\ 5x+4y=13.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 8 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$ we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -14 \\ 5 & 13\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}2 & -14 \\ 5 & 13\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}2 & 8 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2x-3y=-11 \\ 3x-y=11.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$ we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & -11 \\ 3 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}-2 & -11 \\ 3 & 11\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2x-3y=-11 \\ 3x-y=11.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$ we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & -11 \\ 3 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}-2 & -11 \\ 3 & 11\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+5y=15 \\ 2x-3y=-9.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$ we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 15 \\ 2 & -9\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}3 & 15 \\ 2 & -9\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+5y=15 \\ 2x-3y=-9.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$ we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 15 \\ 2 & -9\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}3 & 15 \\ 2 & -9\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x+7y=13 \\ -2x+5y=19.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$ we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 13 \\ -2 & 19\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}4 & 13 \\ -2 & 19\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x+7y=13 \\ -2x+5y=19.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 13 \\ -2 & 19\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}4 & 13 \\ -2 & 19\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$
